title: EPA Section 608 Technician Certification
releaseBlockers: EPA's site notice says commercial use of some content may be protected: confirm every cited EPA page is a US Government work before release
the EPA test topics predate the current rules (leak-repair limits, refrigerants covered): check every card against the current regulation
description: EPA 608: every idea explained before it is tested, every card quoting the source words it rests on.
sourceShort: the EPA's Section 608 pages and 40 CFR Part 82 Subpart F
notice: Section 608 Technician Certification is a requirement of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency under Section 608 of the Clean Air Act and 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F. Tests are given by EPA-approved certifying organisations. This deck is independent and is not affiliated with, sponsored, endorsed or approved by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency or any certifying organisation, and passing it certifies nothing. It uses EPA web pages and the Code of Federal Regulations, which are U.S. Government works. It contains no questions from the EPA test bank.

checks.what: Two independent audits read all 501 cards against 40 CFR Part 82 Subpart F, the EPA's Section 608 pages and the other regulations they quote, word for word as found by the card checker, and checked every card against the current rules rather than the older test topics
checks.result: 2 wrong cards were fixed: both said leak repair covers only ozone-depleting refrigerants, but since 1 January 2026 a separate rule (40 CFR 84.106) covers many HFC appliances; three related cards were scoped to match. 2 unsupported claims, 8 ambiguous cards, 3 unclear ones and 10 minor issues were also fixed.
